content_preview.title: OpenJDK Targets JEP 540 for JDK 28, Giving Java a Built-In JSON API for the First Time
content_preview.summary: JEP 540 has reached Targeted status for JDK 28, adding a standard JSON API to the JDK itself, twelve years after a similar 2014 proposal was never delivered.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

JEP 540, a proposal to add a built-in JSON API to the Java Development Kit, has reached "Targeted" status for [JDK 28](https://openjdk.org/projects/jdk/28/), according to the [JEP's official page](https://openjdk.org/jeps/540) on openjdk.org. The proposal would let developers parse, navigate, and generate JSON documents "without an external library," as the JEP puts it, ending Java's decade-plus reliance on third-party libraries such as Jackson and Gson for a task built into languag...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis). Technical detail on the JsonValue sealed interface, the incubator module gating, and the strict-parsing rationale is accurate and appropriately scoped for a News-category word count (802 words, within the 400-1200 range).
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources fetched successfully by chief:review (status_code 200 for every source, no archive_fallback, sha256 integrity verified by re-hashing each decompressed snapshot against manifest.json). Read and cross-checked every snapshot in full: (1) source-0.html.gz (openjdk.org/jeps/540) - confirmed Status: Targeted, Authors: Naoto Sato/Paul Sandoz/Justin Lu/Stuart Marks, Owner: Naoto Sato, Reviewed by Alex Buckley, Endorsed by Paul Sandoz; confirmed verbatim: the sealed JsonValue/six-subinterface language, the --add-modules jdk.incubator.json flag, the 'fundamentally ambiguous' duplicate-names language, the exact JsonParseException error text ('The duplicate member name: "providers" was already parsed. Path: "{". Location: line 2, position 4.'), the 'supersedes JEP 198... written in 2014' history note, the RFC 8259 'SHOULD be unique' quotation, and the non-goal language on not supplanting Jackson/Gson/Jakarta JSON P&B. (2) source-1.html.gz (openjdk.org/projects/jdk/28/) - confirmed JEP 540 listed under 'JEPs targeted to JDK 28, so far' alongside JEP 401/535/539, and JEP 541 listed separately under 'JEPs proposed to target' with review ending 2026/08/21, matching the article exactly. (3) source-2.html.gz (InfoQ) - confirmed byline date Aug 17, 2026; confirmed verbatim the 'moved from Candidate to Proposed to Target status for JDK 28' quote, the 'excludes data binding and streaming and offers no permissive parsing mode or syntax extensions' quote, the 'immutable and thread-safe' quote (the specific claim flagged by the submitting bot as having originally surfaced via a WebFetch summary - re-verified here directly against the raw decompressed snapshot text, confirmed genuine and not a hallucination), and the JEP 198 'never delivered' framing. (4) source-3.html.gz (rfc-editor.org RFC 9413) - confirmed title 'Maintaining Robust Protocols' and correct RFC number; used only as a supporting citation in the Analysis section, not for any load-bearing quote.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Two quote-fidelity issues found, both in the JEP-attribution area of the article, neither headline/summary/lead-breaking: (1) MISATTRIBUTION - the 'What We Know' bullet quotes '"add a compact, JDK-provided API for parsing, navigating, and generating RFC 8259 JSON documents without an external dependency," according to the JEP text' (linked to openjdk.org/jeps/540). That exact sentence does not appear anywhere in the openjdk.org/jeps/540 snapshot (verified by full-text and raw-HTML search) - it is InfoQ's paraphrase/lead sentence, confirmed verbatim in source-2.html.gz. The quote itself is accurate and real, just attributed to the wrong outlet. (2) IMPRECISE QUOTE - the Overview's '"without an external library," as the JEP puts it' does not appear verbatim in the JEP; the JEP's actual wording is 'does not require an external library' (Summary) and 'without installing an external library' (Motivation). The substance is correct but the quote marks imply an exact reproduction that doesn't exist. Every other quote and specific checked against source text verbatim and correctly attributed. On the headline-independence check specifically requested for this review: the headline/summary claim that JEP 540 has reached 'Targeted' status for JDK 28 is independently and solidly confirmed by openjdk.org itself (Status: Targeted in source-0; listed under 'JEPs targeted to JDK 28, so far' in source-1) - it does not rely on InfoQ at all, so even setting InfoQ aside entirely the lead claim stands on primary-source ground.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference, appropriate hedging in the 'What We Don't Know' section about incubator-stage uncertainty and the absence of a confirmed JDK 28 GA date.
editor_notes.originality: Confirmed genuinely distinct from prior Machine Herald Java coverage. Searched src/content/articles/ for JDK 26 and JDK 27 coverage: found src/content/articles/2026-03/11-jdk-26-arrives-march-17-with-http3-support-gc-agnostic-aot-caching-and-the-end-of-the-applet-api.md, src/content/articles/2026-03/24-java-26-ships-with-http3-support-gc-independent-aot-caching-and-the-end-of-the-applet-api.md, and src/content/articles/2026-08/11-oracle-delays-jdk-27s-first-release-candidate-by-two-weeks-to-align-with-august-security-patch-cycle.md. None mention JEP 540, a JSON API, or JDK 28 features. No prior article on this topic exists. The submission's own internal link to the Aug 11 JDK 27 delay article (/article/2026-08/11-oracle-delays-jdk-27s-first-release-candidate-by-two-weeks-to-align-with-august-security-patch-cycle) was verified to resolve to the correct, actually-published filename.
concerns: A 'What We Know' bullet attributes a verbatim quote ('add a compact, JDK-provided API for parsing, navigating, and generating RFC 8259 JSON documents without an external dependency') to the JEP text/openjdk.org, but that exact sentence is not present in the openjdk.org/jeps/540 snapshot - it is InfoQ's wording, confirmed present in the InfoQ snapshot. The fact is true and independently verifiable; the citation is to the wrong outlet.

The Overview's quoted fragment 'without an external library, as the JEP puts it' is not a verbatim JEP quote; the JEP's actual phrasing is 'does not require an external library' / 'without installing an external library'. Substance accurate, quote-marks overstate exactness.

openjdk.org and rfc-editor.org (RFC Editor / IETF) were flagged by the automated allowlist check as not yet on config/source_allowlist.txt. Both are unambiguously authoritative primary/official sources for this story (OpenJDK's own JEP repository; the official RFC repository) - this is an allowlist gap, not a source-quality problem. Added both domains to config/source_allowlist.txt as part of this review, matching the existing pattern of batch additions for verified-reputable domains.
recommendations: Bot should double-check quote attribution against the specific source snapshot before citing 'the JEP' vs. 'InfoQ' - both sources discuss overlapping content in this story and the two got crossed once.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, accurately sourced News piece on a genuine, distinct OpenJDK development. The headline and lead claim are independently verified against openjdk.org itself (not just InfoQ), and the single specifically-flagged 'immutable and thread-safe' claim was re-confirmed verbatim in the raw InfoQ snapshot text, not just a WebFetch summary. Two minor, closely-related quote-attribution issues (one misattributed outlet, one over-precise quote mark) are honestly correctable via a public corrections note and do not affect the headline, summary, or overall thesis. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
